After breakfast, set out on an excursion to Tierra del Fuego National Park.

It is the world’s southernmost nature reserve and the only national park with a seacoast. The shoreline stretches for about 6 km along the Beagle Channel. The park covers 63,000 hectares.

The tour takes you along the Pipo River and past Mount Susana. You’ll see Ensenada Bay, Redonda Island, Lake Roca, Lapataia Bay, lagoons, a beaver dam, and a forest cabin. Rocky mountains, rivers, valleys, forests, lakes, and the seashore all come together in a small area.

After the excursion, transfer to the airport for your flight to El Calafate. A driver will meet you on arrival and take you to your hotel. In a single day you go from the coast of Tierra del Fuego to the lakes and glaciers of El Calafate, with a striking change of scenery.
A towering blue glacier wall above a lake, with sharp Patagonian peaks behind it
Patagonia: a glacier beside a turquoise lake beneath mountain peaks
El Calafate and the Perito Moreno Glacier

After breakfast, visit the Perito Moreno Glacier in Los Glaciares National Park, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

Around 47 glaciers shape this ancient, icy Patagonian landscape. The best known, Perito Moreno, lies at the southwestern end of Lake Argentino, about 80 km from El Calafate.

The glacier’s front wall rises about 60 m. As Perito Moreno continues to move, large slabs of ice periodically break off and fall into the waters of Rico Bend and the Los Témpanos Channel.

One cycle occurs when the glacier reaches the Magallanes Peninsula and blocks the flow of water. Rico Bend is dammed, and the water level rises by about 35 m. The water gradually cuts its way through the ice until the ice dam finally breaks. This cycle takes about 4–6 years.

An optional glacier ice trek is available for $500 per person. You can walk on the ice and try a cocktail served with ice from Perito Moreno.
